fixes.explanation: A market stall sounds reasonable, baker, but Ruth never mentions one. What she asks for is to go into the fields. She wants to glean heads of grain after someone in whose sight she may find favor.

Ruth is not asking to leave, friend. The foreman says she is the one "…who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab." (Ruth 2:6), and Ruth asks to go into the fields. Moab is where she came from, and Boaz later says she left the land of her birth (Ruth 2:11). Today she is heading for the grain.
Right, baker. Ruth the Moabitess asks to go glean, and Naomi replies, "Go ahead, my daughter…" That is a yes. Ruth heads out into the field.

That's the one, friend. The text says Ruth "…happened to come to the part of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech." Elimelech was Naomi's husband (Ruth 1:2-3), so Boaz is family. Ruth just happened to land in his part.
Not quite, friend. Boaz asks his foreman, "Whose young woman is this?" The foreman answers him. Boaz speaks to Ruth herself after that.
That's right, baker. Boaz turns to the foreman of his harvesters and asks, "Whose young woman is this?" The question goes to the foreman, not to Ruth. Then the foreman tells him who she is.

You got it, baker. The foreman says she "…has continued from morning until now, except that she rested a short time in the shelter." That is steady work with one short rest. Boaz hears all of it before he speaks to her.

A walk back to town isn't part of the offer, friend. Boaz tells her, "…when you are thirsty, go and drink from the jars the young men have filled." The young men already filled those jars. Boaz points her to them.
Yes, baker. The text says Ruth "…ate and was satisfied and had some left over." A full belly plus a portion to spare. I've never seen a better meal.

Yes, friend. Ruth "…brought out what she had saved from her meal and gave it to Naomi." That is the food left over from verse 14, where she "…ate and was satisfied and had some left over." She didn't come home with only grain.

Silver would be a fun plot twist, baker, but there's none in this chapter. The text says Ruth brought out "…what she had saved from her meal…" That's the food left over from her meal in verse 14. She gives it to Naomi.

Not a jar, friend. Ruth picks up the grain and brings out "…what she had saved from her meal…" for Naomi. What she carries is grain and her saved food. Boaz's jars were for her to drink from (Ruth 2:9).
That's right, baker. Naomi says, "The man is a close relative. He is one of our kinsman-redeemers." She says it right after Ruth tells her his name. Family is the piece to hold onto.
Yes, baker. Ruth tells Naomi, "Stay with my young men until they have finished gathering all my harvest." The time is tied to the harvest being finished. No week or day is named.
A week isn't what Ruth reports, friend. She tells Naomi, "Stay with my young men until they have finished gathering all my harvest." The time is tied to the harvest. Nobody mentions a week.

Right, baker. Ruth stays close to Boaz's servant girls "…until the barley and wheat harvests were finished." The passage names both the barley harvest and the wheat harvest. She keeps at it through both.
